subject: Discovery recap: inference cost pressure — FinBank
messages:
From: Alex Reynolds <alex@finbank.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-04-06T15:00:00Z
Subject: Intro / FinBank inference cost constraints (post-call)

Marissa —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from my side: we run a conversational/transactional assistant across FinBank's mobile and web channels. Main constraints we called out on the call:
- Unit economics are under pressure: we see a lot of short, high-frequency requests (avg 12 tokens/request) which drives up per-user cost.
- Current infra: GCP-hosted application layer + internal caching layer; model is a fine-tuned Llama-3-13B variant served in-house today.
- Latency target: p95 < 200ms for user-facing flows.
- Accuracy tolerance: we can accept up to ~3% relative drop for quantized variants but need objective benchmarks.
- Interest in batching/caching and quantization to lower cost; open to Dedicated/Reserved capacity if pricing makes sense.

Next steps from our side: share your cost template and any benchmark data you have; schedule a technical deep-dive with engineering.

I'll loop in our infra lead once we have the cost/pricing details.

Best,
Alex
Alex Reynolds
Director, AI Platform — FinBank
alex@finbank.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Alex Reynolds <alex@finbank.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-04-06T17:10:00Z
Subject: Discovery recap: inference cost pressure — FinBank

Alex — thanks for the conversation today. Below is a concise recap (so we have the same set of expectations) and proposed next steps.

1) Pain points / goals
- High per-token spend driven by many short requests (avg ~12 tokens) — looking to reduce $/MAU without impacting UX.
- Need predictable latency (p95 < 200ms) and tight SLOs.
- Compliance and auditability are mandatory (SOC2 scope).

2) Current stack as discussed
- App + orchestration on GCP
- In-house caching layer for some prefix reuse
- Serving: Llama-3-13B fine-tuned model (single model today)

3) Success criteria (what a win looks like)
- 30-50% reduction in inference unit cost (tokens/op) or clear roadmap to get there.
- Maintain p95 latency < 200ms for core flows.
- Quantized model options that stay within ~2-3% relative quality degradation (measured on your eval set).
- Clear path to production (security/compliance + SLA expectations).

4) Batching / caching expectations
- Interested in prefix/KV caching for repeated conversational prefixes (you estimated ~60-80% prefix reuse on the call).
- Prefer lower-latency batching strategies (continuous small batches rather than large queuing) to avoid tail latency spikes.

5) Quantization openness
- You indicated willingness to test 4-bit/INT8 quantized variants if benchmarks show acceptable quality trade-offs.

6) Next steps
- Attached: Redwood cost model template + SOC2 summary (redwood-cost-model-template.xlsx, redwood-soc2-summary.pdf). Please fill in the usage profile (QPS, avg tokens, prefix reuse estimates).
- Schedule technical deep-dive (engineering + infra): proposed Tue Apr 13 at 10:00 AM ET — does that work?
- We'll provide a preliminary pricing view (Dedicated + burst scenarios) and a proposed quantization benchmark plan ahead of the deep-dive.

If that matches your notes, we'll move forward with the technical call and I’ll ask my team to prepare the pricing scenarios and a short benchmark plan.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Sr. Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com | (650) 555-0123

Attachments: redwood-cost-model-template.xlsx (spreadsheet), redwood-soc2-summary.pdf (summary PDF)
From: Alex Reynolds <alex@finbank.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-04-07T13:02:00Z
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: inference cost pressure — FinBank

Thanks Marissa — that recap is accurate. A couple quick clarifications and asks:
- Apr 13 at 10:00 AM ET works for the deep-dive. I'll invite our infra lead (TBD) and a product owner.
- Can you include a Dedicated pricing view that covers three sizing scenarios: pilot (2-4 GPUs), scale (8-12 GPUs), and enterprise (24+ GPUs) and show expected $/1M tokens for each?
- For quantization: what kind of re-qualification would be required for compliance? Would we need additional audit steps if we move to 4-bit models?

If you can send the preliminary pricing and a short note on compliance impact, we'll prep our internal team.

Appreciate it — Alex
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-04-06T18:05:00Z
Subject: Fwd: Discovery recap: inference cost pressure — FinBank (internal action items)

Looping you both in with the external thread — internal action items: 
- Ben: please prepare Dedicated pricing for FinBank across three scenarios Alex listed (pilot/scale/enterprise). Include reserved capacity vs burst-as-needed pricing and expected $/1M tokens. Add assumptions for batching/caching impact (we should show 0%, 25%, 50% prefix reuse cases).
- Connor: draft a quantization benchmark plan (LLM eval set + regression thresholds) and a short tech runbook for prefix/KV caching we can present on Apr 13. Include expected engineering lift and estimated timeline.
- I'll coordinate schedule with Alex and share the cost template we attached. Also capture any SOC2 implications — tag security if needed.

Please keep this thread updated and put PDFs/benchmarks into the Drive folder (https://drive.google.com/finbank-discussion).

Thanks — Marissa
